rules.sentence: Mycosis fungoides: Presents as erythematous patches, plaques, tumors, or erythrodermic “stages,” most frequently involving non-sun-exposed “bathing suit” areas in older individuals.
Lesions may accompany epidermal atrophy, scaling, or pruritus.
Hypopigmented or hyperpigmented patches/plaques may be present, particularly in patients with skin of color.
It rarely presents in children or adolescents (Mycosis fungoides variants are more common in this population).[63][64]
